artDirection.backgroundPrompt: Build a bold visual hierarchy around one large source-derived anchor, or two main anchors when the confirmed multi-subject plan allows it. Aim for roughly 85–110% of the available image region along the anchor's dominant axis, adjusting to actual source proportions and reserved text zones; this is a starting range along one axis, not a whole-canvas area quota. Establish a large visible focal rectangle before reserving copy. If copy competes with the hero, adjust the composition or choose another compatible layout rather than shrinking the anchor into a small centered sticker. Use a close crop, off-center placement or a form extending past one canvas edge when identifying details remain intact. Give secondary forms clear scale contrast instead of making every element a small equal sticker. Minimal and ink styles use few substantial shapes with useful quiet space. Keep grain, halftone dots and technical marks at their appropriate scale. For information-led academic boards, retain copy priority and use a broad, quiet structural field without inventing a hero or data. Preserve subject identity, anatomy, confirmed count and relationships, the selected medium and approved palette. Keep essential identifying features and required text zones clear.
artDirection.cutoutBackgroundPrompt: Support an oversized, separately movable foreground composition. Generate only the empty substrate and any approved material or graphic decorations. Use a few broad, purposeful fields or one strong supporting graphic gesture where the selected style permits it; preserve quiet space for the planned foreground and text. Keep print grain and technical marks at their appropriate scale, and keep information-led academic backgrounds subordinate to copy. Do not depict extracted subjects, their silhouettes, duplicate fragments or detached body parts. Preserve the selected medium, approved palette and numerical text reservations. The separately generated transparent foreground and its initial rectangles carry the main visual scale.
artDirection.subjectPrompt: Create the confirmed subject as a large, clearly resolved transparent asset with tight, even alpha padding. Preserve its identity, anatomy, pose, functional structures, confirmed count and approved style treatment. Keep confirmed relative scale and relationships inside a grouped subject asset. Do not add a scene, solid background, baked checkerboard, text or extra subjects. Its visible shape will become the dominant anchor in the available image region, with a deliberate initial rectangle chosen after inspection; avoid a tiny subject floating inside a large transparent file.

styles.prompt: Text-free portrait digital graphic for {subject}. Rebuild the supplied subject at high graphic intensity from legible monospaced single ASCII glyphs such as . : + x # on a controlled grid, variable-density filled halftone circles, selective flat silhouettes and negative space. Assign glyph fields and circular screens to specific source forms so their density constructs contour, depth and internal relationships. Preserve three to five identifying anchors and essential perspective; reduce intact photographic material and continuous 3D shading. Distinct glyphs must be recognizable close up and the subject recognizable at thumbnail scale. Default to ASCII plus circles; use pure circles or line-screen reconstruction only when explicitly selected or justified by a documented identity failure. Use approved base {paper}, luminous dominant {ink} and restrained secondary/accent {accent}; do not copy the reference palette or scatter equal contrasting colors. Dark tones clarify cavities and key edges. No generic HUD, circuit boards, binary captions, fake code, random word fragments or unrelated objects. {geometry} No readable poster copy, logos or watermarks.
